title: More effort, worse code
summary: Anthropic ships Claude Opus 5 at half the frontier's price — and the interesting part is the effort dial: turn it up on a small fix and the model over-refactors, so more effort can mean a lower coding score. Then The Stack v3, a 113-terabyte open code corpus, and what it actually takes to turn that pile into five trillion trainable, auditable tokens. Plus a sweep where the open-weights fight finally put its names on paper.

topics: Claude Opus 5 (Anthropic): frontier release priced at $5/M input and $25/M output (same as Opus 4.8), 1M-token context unchanged; Anthropic reports it comes close to Fable 5's frontier intelligence at half Fable's price, and on CursorBench 3.2 at max effort lands within 0.5% of Fable 5's peak at half cost per task; on Frontier-Bench v0.1 agentic terminal coding it more than doubles Opus 4.8 and surpasses all other models; outside coverage (the-decoder) reports ~79% on SWE-bench Pro vs ~69% for Opus 4.8; five effort settings (low/medium/high/xhigh/max); Anthropic positions it as much stronger at verifying its work and iterating. The non-monotonic effort behavior: FrontierCode developer Cheng-Yuan Lee found that at higher effort Opus 5 refactors surrounding code even for a one-character fix (changed exactly one character at low, refactored the whole surrounding block at xhigh), and the benchmark penalizes unsolicited changes — so more effort can lower the coding score; Anthropic's migration guidance now warns against instructions like 'include a final verification step' because it causes over-verification, and disabling thinking with xhigh/max now returns a 400 error

The Stack v3 (BigCode / Hugging Face): open source-code corpus; full corpus 113.7 TB, 770 programming languages, 224M repositories, 43.9B files (GitHub snapshot as of Aug 7 2025); ready-to-train split ~15.9 TB, 713 languages, ~4.9 trillion tokens, ODC-By 1.0 license; seven-stage pipeline (go-enry language detection, ScanCode file-level license detection, MinHash-LSH near-deduplication, quality heuristics, StarPII PII redaction of emails/keys/names/passwords/IPs, Jupyter processing, repo-level grouping); ships no model results — positioned as auditable-provenance infrastructure for open code models, with lead engineer Leandro von Werra framing it partly around open code models for cyber defense; excludes issues/PRs/docs/math that earlier versions bundled and requires respecting original repo terms

threads.name: AI sovereignty and open weights
threads.status: The fight produced formal documents on both sides. A Microsoft-organized open letter, 'Open Weights and American AI Leadership,' signed by 20+ companies (Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, Palantir, Hugging Face), argues against broad restrictions on open-weight models; Axios reports OpenAI and Anthropic taking the opposite side on competitive-risk grounds. Covered as a sweep update, not a dive.
threads.arc: From a floated import ban, to a named accusation with a sanctions threat, to organized counter-lobbying by small companies (the Little Tech Association) — and now to a formal industry coalition letter, with the model-hosting and chip companies and two of the big frontier labs landing on opposite sides on paper.

dives.story: Claude Opus 5, and why more effort made it worse
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone configuring an agentic coding model should care that Opus 5's effort dial is non-monotonic for coding — at higher effort it over-refactors and over-verifies, so the right advice is now 'match effort to how open-ended the task is, not how much you care,' and cap effort at high for surgical edits; the price story (near-frontier at half Fable's cost per task) is real but vendor-reported until reproduced.

dives.story: The Stack v3: cleaning a hundred terabytes of code
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone training or fine-tuning a code model should care that provenance, not benchmark score, is what clears legal review — and The Stack v3 turns 113 TB of GitHub into ~5T auditable tokens via documented dedup, per-file license detection, and PII redaction, making the data layer (where reliability and governance are actually decided) the product; it ships no model results, so it is infrastructure, not a capability claim.

concepts_taught: why a reasoning-effort dial can be non-monotonic for coding: a model tuned to verify and iterate will, given more budget on a small well-scoped task, spend it on unsolicited refactoring/over-verification, which graders penalize as errors

what 'cleaning' a large code corpus actually means: language detection, per-file license detection, MinHash near-deduplication (why dedup prevents a corpus from becoming a popularity contest), quality filtering, and PII redaction — and why provenance/auditability is the payoff rather than raw model quality
